text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
* The European Commission will this week fix 2000 as the deadline for the liberalisation of Portuguese telecommunications.
* Alberto Joao Jardim, head of the autonomous regional authority of Madeira, has suggested creating a company linking the island's three main soccer teams.
* British interested in selling used, non-nuclear submarines to Portugal, the head of the British armed forces Sir Peter Inge told the paper in an interview during a visit to Lisbon.

* Airport company ANA will have to raise tariffs 20 to 30 percent in order to recover a projected loss of revenues of 2.5 percent a year with the expected abolition of "duty free" transactions in the European Union from 1999, ANA sources told the paper.
* All Portuguese banks applied under the so-called "Mateus Plan" to repay tax and social security arrears, an official source told the paper.
